name: perf_sky_composite_inputs
description: Arms the sky composite AND the shared inputs its stages ask for, in ONE scenario, so every number here can be read as a within-run RATIO. That is the whole point of the file: a cross-run comparison of these counts is void, because the frame count is not controlled — a previous A/B of this area moved circ_skyupdate_calls 604->294 and circ_skytarget_calls 2420->1190, arms nothing in the change touches, purely because one run rendered half as many frames. Read instead: stage calls per composite ENTRY (does the discarded-pass skip fire?) and gate calls per composite entry (does the per-pass input cache remove the repeats?). Both denominators come from the same run as their numerator, so the frame count cancels. The gate arms also count callers outside the composite, which is a constant per frame and so shifts both arms equally; the DELTA between arms is still the composite's own. Wide tolerances throughout, and that is not laziness: the absolute counts scale with how many frames the machine managed. Two runs of the SAME build measured 300 cycles and 37 — an 8x spread — while the ratios moved 0.50 to 0.49. Pinning the absolutes was tried and failed on exactly that; the RATIOS are the measurement and the pins exist to record numbers in the report, not to assert one. The _patched probes are the real gate: an unresolved Circinus arm reads zero and is indistinguishable from a method that never ran, which is how a perf scenario passes while verifying nothing.

steps.description: CONTROL, read as a ratio against circ_pf_composite_calls. Vanilla still calls CurSkyTarget twice per SkyManagerUpdate; the skip returns early INSIDE the postfix and must not change this.
THE DENOMINATOR. Every other count here is only meaningful divided by this one. Entries unchanged while executions halve is the whole signature of the discarded-pass skip.
THE SKIP: expect ~0.50 of circ_pf_composite_calls (main: ~1.00). Measured 0.50 on a 300-cycle run and 0.49 on a 37-cycle one.
THE SKIP, second stage as corroboration: ~0.50 of entries (0.50 and 0.47 measured).
Skip AND per-pass cache: ~4.4 per entry against ~9.4 on main. Includes callers outside the composite, so this is not calls-per-pass.
Largest combined win: ~2.5 per entry against ~7.9 on main. IsEnclosed asks it six times a pass on main, once here.
~0.9 per entry against ~2.5 on main: asked twice a pass on main, once here.
